message.content:
The cost of renting an apartment in New York City varies widely depending on the borough, neighborhood, size, and amenities. As of early 2024, here are some rough averages:

| Borough | 1‑bedroom (average) | 2‑bedroom (average) |
|---------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Manhattan | $3,200–$4,500/month | $5,000–$7,500/month |
| Brooklyn | $2,400–$3,800/month | $3,800–$5,500/month |
| Queens | $1,800–$2,900/month | $2,900–$4,200/month |
| Bronx | $1,400–$2,300/month | $2,300–$3,500/month |
| Staten Island | $1,200–$2,000/month | $2,000–$3,000/month |

These figures are averages; luxury apartments or those in highly sought-after neighborhoods (e.g., Tribeca, SoHo, Williamsburg) can command rents well above the upper end of these ranges. Conversely, smaller studios or apartments farther from city centers may fall below the lower end. Rental prices also fluctuate seasonally and can be influenced by market demand, so it's wise to check current listings for the most accurate information.
